blocks.content: Leaching: Downward movement of soluble minerals.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Leaching involves the downward movement of soluble minerals through soil layers.
Eluviation is the removal of materials from the upper soil horizon, while Illuviation is the deposition of materials in the lower horizon.
Calcification is characterized by the accumulation of calcium carbonate in dry regions.
Laterization is a result of intense leaching in tropical climates.
Podzolization takes place in cold humid climates, resulting in acidic soils.

blocks.content: Podzolization: Leaching in cold humid climates producing acidic soils.
Eluviation: Removal of materials from upper horizon.
Illuviation: Deposition of materials in lower horizon.

items: Eluviation vs. Illuviation: Remember Eluviation is removal from the upper horizon, whereas Illuviation is deposition in the lower horizon.

Podzolization occurs specifically in cold, humid regions and produces acidic soils.
